meta.heroTagline: Real-time interaction, embodied AI, and data-driven installations.
meta.heroBio: A practice that builds at the boundary between biology and code — where distributed intelligence, material computation, and live data produce experiences that feel genuinely alive.

featured.title: The H.A.N.D.
featured.desc: An experiment in biological logic — the decentralised neural architecture of the cephalopod translated into a responsive soft-robotic artifact. Each silicone digit operates its own state logic via a distributed finite state machine, communicating laterally rather than reporting to a central brain.
featured.role: Solo research — full system design, fabrication and code. UAL Thesis, Dec 2025.

projects.title: Marine Pulse
projects.latin: A breathing globe driven by ocean data
projects.desc: An interactive installation reimagining ocean waves as breath — alive, rhythmic, ever-changing. Visitors place a marker on a map and a glowing globe reacts instantly with waveforms shaped by real-time marine data from that exact location. Wave height, direction, period, and current modulate the globe's motion and colour in TouchDesigner via OSC/WebSocket.
projects.shortDesc: Real-time ocean data made physically present — wave height modulates the globe's motion and colour.
projects.role: Solo — concept, API pipeline, real-time visual system, on-site installation.

projects.title: Coral Bleaching
projects.desc: An interactive installation where coral grows in response to hand motion. Built with TouchDesigner and MediaPipe, the system visualises the balance between movement and decay. The more the viewer moves, the more coral blooms — until it fades again. On-site, coral was projected onto a globe; a CRT TV distorted the viewer's image as a metaphor for ecological loss.
projects.shortDesc: Grow coral from your hands. Watch it bleach and die. A meditation on ecological loss.
projects.role: TouchDesigner development lead. Pearl (collaborator) designed the web interface.

projects.title: Thalassoscope
projects.latin: Fear of the deep, made tangible
projects.desc: An immersive installation transforming thalassophobia — the fear of deep water — into a sensory encounter. Arduino, motion sensors, and reflective materials detect a viewer's presence and animate servo motors and NeoPixels to simulate eerie underwater activity. Light pulses ripple through mirrored surfaces, suggesting lifeforms lurking just beneath.
projects.shortDesc: Arduino, motion sensors, and NeoPixels simulate the uncanny life lurking in deep water.
projects.role: Solo — concept, physical fabrication, electronics, code.

projects.title: Umwelt
projects.desc: A collaboration inspired by Ed Yong's 'An Immense World'. An interactive rotating cube lets viewers experience the world as bird, bat, dog, and octopus. Each face shows a Unity game scene, projection-mapped onto a physical object using TouchDesigner and Arduino rotary encoder input.
projects.shortDesc: See through the senses of bird, bat, dog, and octopus — each face of a rotating cube a different world.
projects.role: Ideation, octopus scene, shader system, TouchDesigner integration. With Ceci González, Elif Bora, Pearl.

projects.title: The Multi-Minded Shape
projects.desc: A hybrid generative system exploring how perception can shape form. A CNN classifies texture images into conceptual categories — probabilities like 70% Flowing, 30% Gridded — locating a position in the latent space of a 3D mesh autoencoder. The resulting mesh morphs between learned forms. A live camera feed in TouchDesigner tracks viewer motion, triggering shader distortions.
projects.shortDesc: CNN-classified texture probabilities navigate a 3D mesh autoencoder's latent space — form as perception.
projects.role: Solo — full ML pipeline, 3D visualisation, interactive installation. UAL 2024.

projects.title: Generative Plastic Lifeform
projects.desc: An interactive web experience where players become a fish navigating oceans filled with microplastics. Built on the NOAA microplastics dataset: each plastic type triggers colour shifts, recursive textures, or shape distortions. A speculative, critical game-like artwork asking whether adaptation is survival — or surrender.
projects.shortDesc: Navigate an ocean of data. Every microplastic type mutates your body. Is adaptation survival — or surrender?
projects.role: Solo — concept, dataset integration, generative visuals, web experience.
